newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Karachi utility boss, workers protest.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Karachi utility boss, workers protest.

text.p: Gunmen killed the head of Karachi's power utility, along with his driver and guard, on Saturday, prompting protests from electricity workers.

Police said Shahid Hamid, 46, managing director of the state-owned Karachi Electric Supply Corporation (KESC), was shot dead on his way to work by two gunmen who also killed his driver. Hamid's bodyguard died in hospital.
The attack took place in Defence Housing Society area, an affluent district of the southern Pakistani port city. The assailants escaped in a car, police said.
There was no claim of responsibility for the attack and no immediate word on its motive.
Angry KESC employees stopped work and forcibly closed most of the corporation's offices in Karachi when they heard of Hamid's killing, witnesses said.
A KESC spokesman said many groups were "after Hamid", but declined to elaborate.
"We are shocked by the incident. He was our beloved officer and the silent majority was in favour of what he was doing to pull the corporation out of its losses," he added.
Hamid took charge of KESC on December 10, vowing to cut its losses, improve its service and prepare it for privatisation.
The KESC has been fiercely criticised by ordinary people and various lobbies over for the last few months because of long and frequent power cuts in residential and industrial areas.
These grievances have occasionally spilt over into violence when angry citizens attacked KESC offices and employees.
Karachi police chief Mohammad Iqbal told Reuters the provincial government had formed a special three-man police committee to investigate Hamid's murder.

"It is too early to say anything about who killed him or why he was killed. I don't like to speculate," Iqbal said. "The committee comprises our best senior officers. I would be in a better position to say something once it completes its work."
Hamid leaves wife, a son aged 21 and a daughter of 16.
In a separate overnight shooting in the Defence Housing area, police said armed robbers killed a policeman and wounded two when the policemen tried to stop their vehicle.
More than 150 people have been killed in political violence in the southern Pakistani city in the past four months, police say.
